The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The Democratic Party is poised to make a comeback in the U.S.
House come Election Day.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro has the results of the latest NPR PBS News mayor's poll.
Democrats have an eight-point lead among likely voters in what's known as the generic
congressional ballot. That's when pollsters ask who people would vote for in their congressional
district if elections were held today. Historically, that's an indicator of Democrats
likely doing well. In fact, in every midterm election in the 21st century, the party with
the advantage on this question heading into Election Day has made gains. So Democrats are
the favorites to win back control of the House. There is a question, however, of just how big
those gains will be given the structural limitations they face because of redistricting.
Domenico Montanaro, NPR News, Washington.
The midterms are in a week. The University of Florida Election Lab says it's so far,
though more than 32 million people have cast their ballots early. The NPR poll finds that
cost of living remains top of mind among voters. But today the conference board is reporting higher
consumer confidence this month as gas prices eased back. The nonpartisan business membership
and research group says its reading rose to 91.7 from 84.2 last month. Israel is holding an
election widely viewed as the most consequential in the country after the last three years of war
from Tel Aviv. NPR's Daniel Estrin is tracking the voter turnout.
Israel is holding its first national vote since the Hamas attacks of October 7,
2023 and years of war in Gaza, Lebanon and across the region. Those conflicts remain open.
Netanyahu is running for re-election with a promise to join forces with the U.S.
to launch new strikes on Iran if he is re-elected. Most polls have shown Netanyahu and his far right
bloc trailing behind the center-right opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot.
It may take weeks to find out who will be Israel's next prime minister.
Voters are choosing parties running for parliament. After election day,
party leaders will try to assemble a coalition. Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
General Motors is moving its stock listing. NPR's Scott Horsley with details.
General Motors shares have traded on the New York Stock Exchange for
most of the automakers history. But the company announced today GM shares will move to the NASDAQ
next month. The move could showcase the carmaker's technology chops. Walmart made a similar jump last
year. NASDAQ will also be home to shares of anthropic when the artificial intelligence
giant goes public next month. The company hopes to raise as much as $100 billion.
Microsoft is set to report earnings tomorrow. The software company is offering buyouts to more
than a quarter of its workforce to save money for its own AI investments. Scott Horsley, NPR News,
Washington. This is NPR News. More than half of middle school and high school students
use AI chatbots for help with homework and when they're sad, lonely, stressed or overwhelmed.
That according to a new report by the mental health advocacy group JET Foundation.
Here's NPR's Rita Chatterjee. The report sums up the findings of a survey of more than 5,000
middle school and high school students in 21 American states. More than a quarter of the
respondents reported turning to chatbots for relationship or problem solving advice.
The survey also found a link between certain kinds of AI use and poor mental health symptoms,
says psychologist Kayla Anderson. She's a vice president of research and evaluation at the JET
Foundation. Students who used AI for schoolwork or homework had higher levels of loneliness
and history of suicidal thoughts, but not the other outcomes we measured. Like depression
and anxiety, those who use chatbots for companionship or when distressed were more likely to have poorer
mental health overall and lower resilience. Rita Chatterjee, NPR News. Jay-Z's stepping into the
spotlight in the next Super Bowl after helping produce the halftime festivities. Last night,
the National Football League, Apple Music and Rock Nation announced the music mogul would headline.
February 14th, he returns to the California Stadium, where he closed a celebration of the
30th anniversary of Reasonable Doubt, his 1996 debut album that was inducted into the
Grammy Hall of Fame last year. In a statement, Jay-Z says 30 years of music, work and culture
on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true. It's NPR.

topics.text: Democrats hold an eight-point lead on the generic congressional ballot ahead of the midterms
Over 32 million people have cast early ballots ahead of the midterm elections, per the University of Florida Election Lab
Consumer confidence rises to 91.7 from 84.2 as gas prices ease, per the Conference Board
Israel holds its first national election since the October 7 Hamas attacks; Netanyahu trails center-right opposition
General Motors to move its stock listing from the NYSE to the NASDAQ next month
Anthropic plans to go public on NASDAQ next month, seeking to raise as much as $100 billion
Microsoft offers buyouts to over a quarter of its workforce to fund AI investments ahead of earnings
Survey finds over half of middle and high school students use AI chatbots for homework and emotional support
Jay-Z to headline the Super Bowl halftime show at Levi's Stadium on February 14
